en.title: Maximum Pairs with Strictly Higher Frontend Performance
en.description:
There are two groups of n numbers each; choose a frontend and a backend to form a pair, using each element at most once. Only pairs in which the frontend value is strictly greater than the backend value count; maximize their number.

The standard I/O, examples and solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n, the second line contains the frontends, and the third line contains the backends. 1≤n≤100000, values in 1..10^9.
en.explanation: Example 1: pair 3 with 2 and 5 with 4 for 2 pairs; 1 cannot beat any backend. Example 2: equality does not satisfy strictly greater, so there are 0 pairs. Example 3: 10>1, so 1 pair.
hints: Sort each group separately, and pair the current backend with the smallest unused frontend that can beat it.
